record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.context_brief: Characterizing pargoids of projections and idempotents
record.original_question: Characterize: (1) pargoids of projections, meaning idempotents in the full transformation semigroup; (2) pargoids of matrix units; and (3) pargoids of idempotents from the basic classes of semigroups.

evidence.quote:
Problem 7.1. (E.S. Lyapin)

(1) Characterize pargoids of projections (idempotents in the semigroup of all transformations).
(2) Characterize the pargoids of matrix units.
(3) Characterize the pargoids of idempotents of the basic classes of semigroups.

Some classes of pargoids were characterized in the paper [11].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A partial groupoid (pargoid) is a set P equipped with a partial binary operation, i.e. a partial map · : P × P ⇀ P. A semigroup S is called an outer extension of a pargoid P if P ⊆ S and, for all a, b ∈ P with a · b defined in P, the product ab in S equals a · b; equivalently, the partial operation on P is the restriction of the multiplication of S.

Given a semigroup S, its set E(S) of idempotents (elements e ∈ S with e² = e) inherits from S the partial operation defined by: e * f is defined and equals ef whenever e, f ∈ E(S) and ef ∈ E(S). The resulting pargoid is called the pargoid of idempotents of S.

Solve the following characterization problems.

(1) Pargoids of projections. Let X be a set and let T(X) be the full transformation semigroup on X (all maps X → X under composition). The idempotents of T(X) are called projections of X. Give an abstract characterization, in purely pargoid-theoretic terms, of those pargoids that are isomorphic to the pargoid of idempotents of T(X) for some set X.

(2) Pargoids of matrix units. For a set I, the matrix-unit semigroup on I is the set M(I) = (I × I) ∪ {0} with multiplication (i, j)(k, l) = (i, l) if j = k and 0 otherwise (and 0 absorbing). Characterize, in pargoid-theoretic terms, those pargoids that arise as the pargoid of idempotents (equivalently, of matrix units together with 0) of M(I) for some set I.

(3) Pargoids of idempotents of basic classes of semigroups. For each of the standard classes of semigroups (e.g. groups, completely simple semigroups, completely 0-simple semigroups, inverse semigroups, regular semigroups, commutative semigroups, bands), give an intrinsic abstract characterization of those pargoids which occur, up to isomorphism, as the pargoid of idempotents of some semigroup in the given class.
